decision.explanation: The claim posits that Tazemetostat shows sensitivity/response in pancreas lymphoma with the EZH2 Y407I variant. The available evidence from pmid-25493630 supports the use of an EZH2 inhibitor (EPZ-6438, which is Tazemetostat) in EZH2-mutant germinal center non-Hodgkin lymphomas (NHL), specifically citing the Y646F variant in the WSU-DLCL2 model. The evidence does not support the specific disease 'pancreas lymphoma' nor the specific variant 'Y407I'. The evidence direction is supportive of efficacy (DOES_NOT_SUPPORT in the claim is incorrect relative to the evidence which shows synergy/TGI). Therefore, the claim requires revision regarding the disease (to germinal center NHL or similar EZH2-mutant lymphoma context) and the variant (to Y646F or generally EZH2 mutant), and the evidence direction (should be SUPPORTS, not DOES_NOT_SUPPORT).

citations.quote: We report here that combining EPZ-6438 with CHOP in preclinical cell culture and mouse models results in dramatic synergy for cell killing in EZH2 mutant germinal center NHL cells . . . Finally, tumor growth inhibition was assessed in 3 different EZH2 mutant lymphoma xenograft models (materials and methods section 6). . . . In WSU-DLCL2 xenograft bearing mice, tumor growth inhibition (TGI) was achieved at all EPZ-6438 doses and schedules employed, and was better than CHOP alon . . . EPZ-6438/CHOP combinations show enhanced anti-tumor activity compared to single agents in several EZH2 mutant
lymphoma xenograft models. . . . WSU-DLCL2 (EZH2 Y646F) xenograft-bearing mice were treated for 28 days as indicated.
